message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file noise‑complaint reports directly with the City’s local authorities. Here’s how you can do it: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go | |------|------------|-------------| | **1** | Identify the source of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). | Gather details: time, location, description, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). | | **2** | File the complaint. | • **Online:** Use the City of Atlanta’s “Report a Problem” portal (https://www.atlantaga.gov/portal/).
• **Phone:** Call the City’s Noise Complaint Hotline at **(404) 876‑1234** (24 hrs). | | **3** | Follow up. | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. You can track the status on the portal or call the hotline. | | **4** | If unresolved, contact your local council member. | Find your council district and representative via the City’s “Find Your Representative” tool (https://www.atlantaga.gov/representatives). | **Key Points** * Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 5 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets limits on decibel levels and defines prohibited activities. * Complaints can be made for both residential and commercial noise violations. * The City’s Department of Public Safety typically handles enforcement after a complaint is filed. If you’re unsure which council district you belong to, use the “Find Your Representative” tool on the City’s website. Once you have your district, you can also email or call your council member’s office to request assistance or follow‑up on the complaint.
